nodes.title: Finite satisfiability
nodes.statement: A set Γ of formulas is finitely satisfiable if every finite Δ ⊆ Γ has a model.
nodes.context: Language L is fixed. Γ is a set of first-order formulas.
assumptions: Γ is a set of L-formulas

nodes.title: Compactness transfer theorem
nodes.statement: If Γ is finitely satisfiable, then Γ is satisfiable.
nodes.context: Work in a first-order language L.
nodes.proofSketch: Use finite satisfiability to build compatible finite models, then pass to a global model.
nodes.formalCode:
theorem compactness_transfer
  (Γ : Set Formula)
  (h : finitely_satisfiable Γ) :
  satisfiable Γ := by
  sorry

subgoals.title: Build the limiting model
subgoals.detail: Use an ultraproduct or a syntactic Henkin construction.

subgoals.title: Show every φ ∈ Γ holds
subgoals.detail: Track finite satisfaction through the construction.

symbols.meaning: Proof that Γ is finitely satisfiable

nodes.title: Finite model compatibility
nodes.statement: For any finite Δ ⊆ Γ, there exists a model MΔ satisfying every formula in Δ.
nodes.proofSketch: Apply the definition of finite satisfiability to Δ.

subgoals.title: Check notation scope
subgoals.detail: Make sure MΔ is not used outside the finite context.

nodes.title: Reduce to library compactness
nodes.statement: Try proving the target theorem by specializing a known compactness theorem.
nodes.context: This may be circular depending on the theorem budget.
nodes.proofSketch: If the library theorem has the exact statement, specialize it to Γ.
assumptions: A library compactness theorem is available

subgoals.title: Check circularity
subgoals.detail: Verify whether the imported theorem is stronger than the target.
